Tamil Nadu previously passed a bill in 2021 seeking an exemption from NEET, but it remains pending without presidential approval. The current resolution highlights concerns over repeated paper leaks and irregularities in NEET, including the cancellation of the exam in May due to a leak. It also

references student suicides linked to exam-related stress.  The resolution calls for the central government to amend the National Medical Commission Act and related laws to eliminate NEET as the national standard for medical admissions.

Medical education experts remain divided on the issue. Some argue that scrapping NEET would return the country to a time of multiple, inconsistent state-level examinations, increasing opportunities for malpractice and creating unequal standards across regions. Others propose reforming the

existing system rather than eliminating it entirely, suggesting improvements such as stronger digital security measures, artificial intelligence monitoring, and conducting the exam twice annually to reduce student stress.

Supporters of retaining a centralized examination system emphasize that it provides a uniform benchmark for students from different educational boards and enables transparent counseling processes. They also advocate for measures such as publishing answer keys, offering free preparation materials
in regional languages, and implementing time-bound grievance resolution mechanisms.
